briefing.headline: Midterms, Brexit debates and devolution tensions dominate politics
briefing.overview: US midterm elections and a Supreme Court ruling on ballot eligibility are in focus, while UK parties grapple with immigration reforms and devolution proposals. Both sides of the Atlantic see intense debate over governance and rights.

stories.title: Supreme Court blocks Trump bid on California ballots
stories.what_happened: The US Supreme Court rejected the Trump administration’s request to set aside 20,000 California ballots it said were likely cast by non‑citizens. The decision was issued quickly on 2 Nov 2026.
stories.why_it_matters: It shows the judiciary’s role in checking executive power, a key point in the A‑level study of the US courts. It also highlights how courts can influence election outcomes.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: The Court upheld electoral integrity by preventing unlawful ballot removal.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: The decision was seen as partisan, protecting votes that the administration claimed were fraudulent.

key_term.definition: The power of courts to assess the legality of actions by the executive or legislature.

stories.exam_use: Use as evidence of judicial independence in an essay on the US courts’ checks on the executive.

stories.title: Labour ends power‑sharing with Greens over Zionism dispute
stories.what_happened: Labour’s National Executive Committee announced it will cut ties with Green councillors in 11 councils because of a disagreement over Zionism policy. The move was reported on 2 Nov 2026.
stories.why_it_matters: The case illustrates intra‑party conflict and the impact of party discipline on local governance, relevant to the AQA topic of political parties.

perspectives.label: From Labour supporters
perspectives.text: The decision protects the party’s core values and avoids association with controversial positions.

perspectives.label: From Green supporters
perspectives.text: The cut is viewed as undemocratic and damaging to progressive coalition building.

key_term.definition: The extent to which party members are expected to follow official party policy.

stories.exam_use: Cite as an example of party cohesion challenges in an essay on UK political parties.

stories.title: Burnham proposes greater devolution to regions and cities
stories.what_happened: Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced a plan to transfer more powers to regional and city authorities across the UK. The proposal was reported on 3 Nov 2026.
stories.why_it_matters: It raises questions about the balance of power between the central government and devolved administrations, a core issue in the UK Constitution syllabus.

perspectives.label: From the left
perspectives.text: Devolution is seen as a way to bring decision‑making closer to citizens.

perspectives.label: From the right
perspectives.text: Critics warn it could fragment national unity and weaken central authority.

perspectives.label: From Welsh officials
perspectives.text: Some argue the plan does not go far enough for Wales.

key_term.definition: The statutory transfer of powers from the central government to regional or local bodies.

stories.exam_use: Use to discuss arguments for and against devolution in a constitutional essay.

stories.title: UK and EU reach draft food‑export deal
stories.what_happened: Britain and the European Union agreed a draft arrangement to remove Brexit‑related red tape on food exports, ahead of a summit later in November. Reported on 3 Nov 2026.
stories.why_it_matters: The deal reflects ongoing negotiations over the post‑Brexit relationship, illustrating how international agreements affect domestic policy and trade.

perspectives.label: Pro‑deal supporters
perspectives.text: The agreement will boost trade and reduce costs for farmers.

perspectives.label: Skeptics
perspectives.text: Some argue it compromises UK sovereignty over food standards.

key_term.definition: A negotiated pact between two or more states governing the terms of trade.

stories.exam_use: Reference in an essay on the impact of Brexit on UK‑EU relations.

stories.title: US midterm elections could shift congressional control
stories.what_happened: On 3 Nov 2026 voters cast ballots in midterm elections that will determine whether Republicans retain control of Congress or Democrats gain a majority. Coverage highlighted the stakes for both parties.
stories.why_it_matters: The outcome will affect legislative agendas and the balance of power, key concepts in the study of US elections and party systems.

perspectives.label: Republican view
perspectives.text: Winning will allow continuation of the administration’s policy agenda.

perspectives.label: Democratic view
perspectives.text: Gaining seats would enable checks on the President and advance their platform.

key_term.definition: Elections held halfway through a President’s term to elect members of Congress.

stories.exam_use: Use as a contemporary example when discussing how elections shape US legislative power.

compare.uk: The UK relies on an uncodified constitution, meaning constitutional principles are spread across statutes, conventions and judicial decisions.
compare.us: The US has a single written constitution that sets out the structure of government and protects individual rights.
compare.insight: The contrast shows how a codified document can provide clearer legal limits, while an uncodified system offers flexibility but can create ambiguity.

ideas_lens.text: Liberal thinkers such as John Locke argue for limited government and protection of individual rights; the US Supreme Court’s refusal to discard ballots reflects a liberal commitment to procedural fairness, while the UK’s devolution plan seeks to empower local choice, another liberal principle.

exam_question.question: Assess the extent to which devolution proposals can address regional disparities in the UK.
exam_question.tip: Compare arguments for greater regional power with concerns about national cohesion, using recent devolution proposals as evidence.
